=== 15-node-q-11.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.

Does the product also provide mains socket outlets (power strip, extension lead) in addition to its charging ports?
A block that combines several sockets of heading 8536 to distribute the current may fall under another heading; with a converter, it is a composite machine within the meaning of note 3 to Section XVI, which this tree does not decide.
Heading 8536 · Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504
Yes

8507.60 Lithium-ion accumulators
Rechargeable lead-acid, nickel-cadmium or nickel-metal hydride battery
Out of scope Pack of non-rechargeable cells, or lead-acid, nickel-cadmium or nickel-metal hydride accumulator: the product falls under neither subheading 8507 60 nor subheading 8507 80. Primary cells are not accumulators of heading 8507 (US ruling N342905 retains 8506 10) and the named accumulators have their own subheadings. Carry data, video or sound between devices (cable, adapter, hub, docking station, network dongle)
Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.
Heading 8544 · Heading 8536
Yes
Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.
Chapter 84, note 6(D) · Chapter 84, note 6(D)(2) · Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8517
No network or radio interface
According to the datasheet, for which devices is the product stated (upstream port, drivers, compatibility)?
Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

=== 16-node-q-11-text.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.
General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · Heading 8544 · Heading 8536 · Subheadings 8544 42 and 8544 49 (common dash) · Subheadings 8536 61 and 8536 69 (common dash) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6
Flexible cable of insulated conductors, fitted with connectors (USB, Lightning, HDMI, jack, power)
8544.42 Other electric conductors, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V, fitted with connectors
Coaxial cable fitted with connectors (central core surrounded by a second conductor)
Out of scope Coaxial cable, wiring set for vehicles or optical fibre cable made up of individually sheathed fibres: the product stays in heading 8544 but outside subheadings 8544 42 and 8544 49. Subheadings 8544 20, 8544 30 and 8544 70 are not in the text repository and this tree does not cover them.
Cable or wiring set designed to be fitted in a vehicle, an aircraft or a ship
Out of scope Coaxial cable, wiring set for vehicles or optical fibre cable made up of individually sheathed fibres: the product stays in heading 8544 but outside subheadings 8544 42 and 8544 49. Subheadings 8544 20, 8544 30 and 8544 70 are not in the text repository and this tree does not cover them.
Optical fibre cable in which each fibre is individually sheathed, without a transceiver
Out of scope Coaxial cable, wiring set for vehicles or optical fibre cable made up of individually sheathed fibres: the product stays in heading 8544 but outside subheadings 8544 42 and 8544 49. Subheadings 8544 20, 8544 30 and 8544 70 are not in the text repository and this tree does not cover them.
Rigid block of plugs and sockets with no length of cable, no switch and no fuse
8536.69 Plugs and sockets, other, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V
Box with mechanical buttons that selects an input
Out of scope Mechanical selector without electronics: a switch of subheading 8536 50, not covered by this tree.
Yes: alternating to direct current, direct to direct current (12 V to 5 V) or inductive charging with rectification
Does the product also provide mains socket outlets (power strip, extension lead) in addition to its charging ports?
A block that combines several sockets of heading 8536 to distribute the current may fall under another heading; with a converter, it is a composite machine within the meaning of note 3 to Section XVI, which this tree does not decide.
Heading 8536 · Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504

Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

=== 17-node-c-0.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.

Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. Heading 8544 · Heading 8536
Yes
Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

=== 18-node-c-17.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes

Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.

Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.

Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

=== 20-node-out-of-scope.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.

Heading 8544 · Heading 8536
Yes
Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

According to the datasheet, for which devices is the product stated (upstream port, drivers, compatibility)?
Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 3 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Subheading 8507 60 · Subheading 8507 80 · Section XVI, note 3
No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.
Heading 8504 · Subheading 8504 40 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 6 · Heading 8536 · Heading 8544
No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it
How is the product without electronics constructed?
Rule 1 classifies according to the terms of the headings: heading 8544 covers insulated wire and cable whether or not fitted with connectors, heading 8536 plugs, sockets and switches, and rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level.

Carry data, video or sound between devices (cable, adapter, hub, docking station, network dongle)
Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.
Heading 8544 · Heading 8536
Yes
Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.
Chapter 84, note 6(D) · Chapter 84, note 6(D)(2) · Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8517
No network or radio interface
According to the datasheet, for which devices is the product stated (upstream port, drivers, compatibility)?
Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.
Chapter 84, note 6(C), first paragraph · Chapter 84, note 6(E) · Heading 8471 · Heading 8543
Computers or tablets, with no other device stated (Windows, macOS, Linux compatibility, USB or Thunderbolt host port)

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

=== 22-refused-edit.txt ===
Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.

No battery or cells
Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.

No: the product connects contacts or conducts the current without modifying it

Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

value: Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

8504.40 Static converters
Carry data, video or sound between devices (cable, adapter, hub, docking station, network dongle)
Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

      } else if (product.construction_passive === 'faisceau_vehicule') {

      } else if (product.construction_passive === 'fibre_optique') {
        return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Coaxial cable, wiring set for vehicles or optical fibre cable made up of individually sheathed fibres: the product stays in heading 8544 but outside subheadings 8544 42 and 8544 49.       } else if (product.construction_passive === 'bloc_fiches_prises') {
        return '853669'; // Plugs and sockets, other, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V
      } else if (product.construction_passive === 'commutateur_mecanique') {
        return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Mechanical selector without electronics: a switch of subheading 8536 50, not covered by this tree.
      }
    }
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'porter_completer') {
    // Device it connects to  [h8473, sh847330, s16-n1, s16-n1g, s16-n2, s16-n2b]
    if (product.appareil_hote == null) return ask('appareil_hote');
    if (product.appareil_hote === 'ordinateur') {
      return '847330'; // Parts and accessories of the machines of heading 8471
    } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'mixte') {
      return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Product stated for a phone, a vehicle, a console, a medical device, audio or video devices, or for several types of device at once, and not for the computer alone.     } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'audio_video') {

The competing headings (8517, 8522, 8529, 8537, 8543, 9504) depend on the host device and this tree does not decide between them.
    } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'autre') {
      return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Product stated for a phone, a vehicle, a console, a medical device, audio or video devices, or for several types of device at once, and not for the computer alone. For parts, note 2(b) to Section XVI refers to heading 8517 those of the goods of headings 8517 and 8525 to 8528 and to heading 8529 those of heading 8524; articles of Chapter 95 fall outside the section (note 1(p)). The competing headings (8517, 8522, 8529, 8537, 8543, 9504) depend on the host device and this tree does not decide between them.
    }
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'autre') {
    return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // The principal function is neither power supply nor connection (hand warmer that also recharges a phone, luminaire, loudspeaker): the product is classified according to that function, under a heading that this tree does not cover.
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'aucune_dominante') {
    return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // No function prevails: for a machine of Chapter 84, note 8 refers to heading 8479; otherwise, after rules 3(a) and 3(b), rule 3(c) takes the heading which occurs last among those which equally merit consideration. This tree does not make that determination.
  }

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. // Generated from the tree. Do not edit here: edit the tree.
function classify(product) {
  // Principal function  [s16-n3, s16-n5, rgi-1, rgi-3, rgi-3a, rgi-3b]
  if (product.fonction_principale == null) return ask('fonction_principale');
  if (product.fonction_principale === 'alimenter') {
    return '850440'; // Static converters
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'transmettre_signaux') {

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product contain a chip or a circuit that converts, regenerates, distributes or switches the signal?
Heading 8544 covers insulated conductors whether or not fitted with connectors, and heading 8536 the apparatus for making connections to or switching electrical circuits. A product that processes the signal is described by neither of these two heading texts and is classified according to its function.

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.

Yes

Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.

Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.

Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function.     } else if (product.genere_electricite === false) {

      } else if (product.construction_passive === 'bloc_fiches_prises') {
        return '853669'; // Plugs and sockets, other, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V
      } else if (product.construction_passive === 'commutateur_mecanique') {
        return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Mechanical selector without electronics: a switch of subheading 8536 50, not covered by this tree.
      }
    }
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'porter_completer') {
    // Device it connects to  [h8473, sh847330, s16-n1, s16-n1g, s16-n2, s16-n2b]
    if (product.appareil_hote == null) return ask('appareil_hote');
    if (product.appareil_hote === 'ordinateur') {
      return '847330'; // Parts and accessories of the machines of heading 8471
    } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'mixte') {
      return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Product stated for a phone, a vehicle, a console, a medical device, audio or video devices, or for several types of device at once, and not for the computer alone. For parts, note 2(b) to Section XVI refers to heading 8517 those of the goods of headings 8517 and 8525 to 8528 and to heading 8529 those of heading 8524; articles of Chapter 95 fall outside the section (note 1(p)). The competing headings (8517, 8522, 8529, 8537, 8543, 9504) depend on the host device and this tree does not decide between them.
    } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'audio_video') {
      return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Product stated for a phone, a vehicle, a console, a medical device, audio or video devices, or for several types of device at once, and not for the computer alone. For parts, note 2(b) to Section XVI refers to heading 8517 those of the goods of headings 8517 and 8525 to 8528 and to heading 8529 those of heading 8524; articles of Chapter 95 fall outside the section (note 1(p)). The competing headings (8517, 8522, 8529, 8537, 8543, 9504) depend on the host device and this tree does not decide between them.
    } else if (product.appareil_hote === 'autre') {
      return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // Product stated for a phone, a vehicle, a console, a medical device, audio or video devices, or for several types of device at once, and not for the computer alone. For parts, note 2(b) to Section XVI refers to heading 8517 those of the goods of headings 8517 and 8525 to 8528 and to heading 8529 those of heading 8524; articles of Chapter 95 fall outside the section (note 1(p)). The competing headings (8517, 8522, 8529, 8537, 8543, 9504) depend on the host device and this tree does not decide between them.
    }
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'autre') {
    return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // The principal function is neither power supply nor connection (hand warmer that also recharges a phone, luminaire, loudspeaker): the product is classified according to that function, under a heading that this tree does not cover.
  } else if (product.fonction_principale === 'aucune_dominante') {
    return OUT_OF_SCOPE; // No function prevails: for a machine of Chapter 84, note 8 refers to heading 8479; otherwise, after rules 3(a) and 3(b), rule 3(c) takes the heading which occurs last among those which equally merit consideration. This tree does not make that determination.
  }
}

Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Revert to the reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.

Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.

Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Revert to the reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.
Section XVI, note 3 · Section XVI, note 5 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 1 · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3 (introductory sentence) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(a) · General rules for the interpretation of the Combined Nomenclature, rule 3(b)
Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.
Section XVI, note 3 · Heading 8504 · Heading 8507 · Chapter 85, note 2
Yes
Out of scope Charger that generates its own electricity (solar, hand crank): a composite machine that this tree does not decide. Note 2 to Chapter 85 excludes headings 8501 to 8504 for goods described in heading 8541; the texts of headings 8501 and 8541 are not in the repository. US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.
No
Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.

Does the product change the nature of the current (alternating to direct, direct to direct, inductive charging with rectification)?
Heading 8504 covers electrical transformers, static converters and inductors; subheading 8504 40 takes only static converters (rule 6). A product that only connects contacts is a cable of heading 8544 or connection apparatus of heading 8536.

Which network or communication interfaces does the product carry (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile network, serial link, transceivers on fibre or copper)?
Note 6(D)(2) to Chapter 84 excludes from heading 8471 apparatus for the transmission or reception of data when presented separately, even if it meets the conditions of note 6(C); where this function sits alongside other functions, note 3 to Section XVI takes the principal function. Reading adopted by this tree, drawn from rulings and not from the text of the note: a hub, a docking station or a display adapter without a network interface is not treated as transmission apparatus (H348342, N292574). Ruling N289786 reads the note the other way.

Note 6(C) to Chapter 84 regards as a unit of heading 8471 the article that meets three conditions at once: being of a kind solely or principally used in an automatic data-processing system, being connectable to the central processing unit, and being able to accept or deliver data in a form which can be used by the system. Apparatus performing a specific function other than data processing follows note 6(E). The tree checks only the first condition, through the devices that the datasheet states.

Interpretation tree · Cleo
Interpretation tree

Power supplies and chargers for electronic devices (mains adapters, USB chargers, wireless chargers, power banks), docking stations, port replicators, USB hubs, connection adapters and cables fitted with connectors for computers and phones, for a voltage not exceeding 1 000 V. The rule is data: edit a branch and everything is recomputed.

Classify a product
Chargers, power banks, docking stations, hubs, adapters and cables for computers and phones
Revert to the reference tree
Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), six digits only, national code not established. Drafted by AI from the cited texts, not reviewed by a customs declarant. Orange bar: edited node.
Which function do the datasheet and the packaging state first for this product?
Where a product combines several machines or several functions, note 3 to Section XVI classifies it, unless the context otherwise requires, according to the principal function. For a composite article that is not a machine, rule 3(b) takes the component which gives the essential character, if rule 3(a) is not sufficient. Limit: rule 1 puts the terms of the headings before this test, and a single-function product (cable, block of plugs, battery alone) has no principal function to establish; the tree nevertheless asks this question of every product and takes as an indication the function that the datasheet states first.

Supply energy to another device: power it, charge it or store electricity for it
Does the product generate its own electricity (solar panel, dynamo, hand crank)?
A charger that generates its own current combines a generator and other functions; note 3 to Section XVI classifies it according to the principal function, which this tree does not decide.

Yes

US ruling N319727 retains subheading 8504 40 for a solar charging station with a battery.

Does the product contain a battery or cells whose energy is delivered to the connected device, and of what type?
Heading 8507 covers electric accumulators, including those presented with ancillary components which contribute to storing and supplying energy or protect them from damage (note 3 to Chapter 85); rule 6 then decides between subheadings at the same level according to the technology. Limit: the note cites neither a converter nor an inverter among these components, and the tree does not compare headings 8504 and 8507 for a power station with mains outputs.
